name: Renaissance Global Ltd
title: Renaissance Global Ltd - 532923 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: H1 FY27 PAT up ~92% YoY to INR52 crores on operating revenue of INR1,329 crores (+25%); net debt cut to INR199 crores.
summary.overview: Renaissance Global reported Q2 FY27 operating revenue of INR639 crores (+20% YoY) and H1 operating revenue of INR1,329 crores (+25% YoY), with H1 EBITDA up 21% to INR101 crores at a 7.6% margin. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow hit a record INR280 crores and net debt fell 42% YoY to INR199 crores. Management is exiting high-working-capital customer-brand accounts (about INR400 crores of run-rate revenue), which weighs on customer-brand growth and gross margin in the near term. Own brands Jean Dousset and With Clarity are guided to about INR375 crores of FY27 revenue, with INR172 crores already booked in H1.

financial_highlights.change: vs outflow of INR83 crores in H1 FY26
record; prior peak INR229 crores in FY23

financial_highlights.value: Reduced by 54 days YoY; target ~180 days

segments.name: Own brands (Jean Dousset + With Clarity)
segments.commentary: Own brands grew 39% in the quarter per management; Jean Dousset above 50% growth and With Clarity mid-20s. FY27 guidance ~INR375 crores (With Clarity ~INR220 crores, Jean Dousset ~INR160-175 crores), with INR172 crores achieved in H1; own brands' CAGR since FY22 is 66%.

segments.name: Customer brands
segments.commentary: Exiting accounts with ~INR400 crores of run-rate revenue that are 100% consignment and high working capital; FY27 segment revenue guided to ~INR1,700-1,800 crores, with FY28 run-rate ~INR1,400-1,500 crores. Segment EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 6-8% range.

segments.name: Licensed brands (House of Disney)
segments.commentary: Management says it remains a pillar of the D2C portfolio; no specific numbers given on the call. Advertising spend for licensed DTC about 30% of sales (~INR125 crores, per management).

capex_capacity: Jean Dousset boutiques: 4 operating (Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Boston; Boston opened Nov 4, 2026); 4 more planned in Washington D.C., Chicago, Miami and Dallas over coming months, taking network to 8 by end FY27.
Store economics: target INR25-30 crores annual sales per boutique; payback ~12-15 months; capex plus inventory ~INR10-12 crores per store; inventory ~INR5 crores per store.
Manufacturing: currently in-house manufacturing ~25% of Jean Dousset sales; plan to move fully in-house over 12-18 months. Bhavnagar facility shut; capacity constraints cited.
Inventory ~INR1,000 crores+, of which 30-50% estimated to be consignment inventory with customers.
demand_pricing: Jean Dousset average order value ~USD5,500 (store ~INR7 lakh, online ~INR4 lakh); roughly 50% made-to-order; gross margin 68%; contribution margin ~43% on a USD2.6 million per-store model (pre-advertising).
With Clarity AOV ~USD2,500, gross margin 63% after discounts and shipping; marketplace model only for lab diamonds (vendors list stones, ~85% gross margin on stone sales per management).
Legacy Jean Dousset stores growing high single-digit same-store sales, mainly volume; prices stable. New York did north of INR30 crores in year one.
Advertising: FY26 spend ~INR149 crores; Jean Dousset ~25% of sales in FY26, guided to 17-18% in FY27; With Clarity mid-30s%; licensed ~30%.
Competition: Brilliant Earth and Blue Nile in lab-grown online; Jean Dousset positioned in luxury lab-grown white space with no direct lab-grown luxury peer per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 EBITDA margin fall to 7.6% from 7.9% despite D2C growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to exits from customer-brand accounts with long working capital cycles, which carry costs and clear inventory at lower gross margin; H2 is seasonally stronger and margins should improve, with a clean balance sheet entering FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why carry gross debt when cash flow is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of debt is about 6-7%; company holds ~INR383 crores of cash and investments for possible acquisitions and for funding the next four Jean Dousset stores, and can repay at any time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the customer-brand working capital release on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan stands: it avoided ~INR417 crores of working capital versus constant intensity over 12 months; the exits process began ~6 months ago and inventory is being sold down.

qa_highlights.question: Forex losses persist even though most revenue is export-linked.
qa_highlights.answer: Darshil Shah said USD-denominated borrowings (about INR550-600 crores of gross debt, majority of gross borrowings) are revalued at current rates, driving much of the forex loss; Sumit Shah suggested judging gross margin after forex adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: Will customer-brand margins rise after exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected to stay in the 6-8% range; group margin to improve through mix shift toward higher-margin D2C segments.

qa_highlights.question: Jean Dousset store maturity and FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: New York already well above INR25 crores; San Francisco expected to reach around USD2.5 million next year; maturity takes 14-25 weeks; tracking metric is 25 appointments a week.

risks_watch: Customer-brand revenue shrinking by ~INR400 crores run-rate as exits proceed; growth decelerating Q1 to Q2 and expected to continue in H2.
Forex: ~INR20 crores forex loss in the quarter; ~INR550-600 crores USD-denominated borrowings create revaluation exposure; rupee ~10-15% weaker YoY.
Bullion sales (INR146 crores in H1) to continue through FY27; accounting methodology change with auditors expected in FY28.
Jean Dousset in-house manufacturing transition (from ~25% today) expected to take 12-18 months; higher traded goods share in the interim.
Acquisition plans and deleveraging target (~INR100 crores net debt by 2030) compete for cash; no acquisition specifics given.
Consignment share of customer-brand inventory unclear; management said it would follow up on the figure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Jean Dousset store economics and cash flow, but evasive on specifics: declined to quantify consignment share, employee cost reduction, and acquisition targets, and gave ranges rather than figures on margins and customer-brand revenue.
key_quotes: So we're extremely happy with sort of the 2 new stores that have opened up now.
So in effect, we've saved INR417 crores of working capital because had the business been at the same working capital intensity, we would have needed far more capital than we actually needed to use.
The unique selling point of Jean Dousset is that customers make appointments.
guidance_outlook: Own brands (Jean Dousset + With Clarity) FY27 revenue guided to about INR375 crores, of which INR172 crores was achieved in H1; split roughly INR220 crores With Clarity and INR160-175 crores Jean Dousset.

Customer brands FY27 revenue guided to about INR1,700-1,800 crores, with FY28 run-rate about INR1,400-1,500 crores; customer-brand EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 6-8% range, with group margin improving through mix shift.

Exiting customer accounts with about INR400 crores of run-rate revenue (100% consignment, high working capital); exits to run through rest of FY27, with the run-rate reduction complete by year-end as inventory sells down; growth to decelerate in H2.

Jean Dousset network to reach 8 boutiques by end FY27 (4 more in Washington D.C., Chicago, Miami and Dallas over coming months); target INR25-30 crores annual sales per store; payback 12-15 months; Jean Dousset FY28 sales expected to be meaningfully higher; San Francisco expected to reach about USD2.5 million next year.
Working capital cycle target of about 180 days; net debt target about INR100 crores by 2030; long-term ambition of INR1,000 crores D2C business by FY29.

Bullion sales to continue for rest of FY27; accounting methodology change with auditors expected in FY28. Jean Dousset in-house manufacturing (about 25% today) to reach full in-house over 12-18 months. Forex losses to be judged after adjusting gross margin; management did not give a forex outlook number.

adds.what: 4 Jean Dousset boutiques opened (Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Boston; Boston opened Nov 4, 2026)
4 more Jean Dousset boutiques planned (Washington D.C., Chicago, Miami, Dallas), taking network to 8 by end FY27

growth.why: Own brands guided to ~INR375 crores FY27 with INR172 crores achieved in H1 and 4 more boutiques by end FY27, but customer brands (~INR400 crores run-rate) are being exited with growth decelerating in H2, so group growth outlook is flat-to-modest and no total group revenue growth % is guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 7.6% vs 7.9% prior year, but management expects H2 seasonal strength and mix shift to D2C, with customer-brand margins guided at 6-8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Four Jean Dousset boutiques are committed (Boston opened Nov 4, 2026) with four more planned in Washington D.C., Chicago, Miami and Dallas, taking the network to 8 by end FY27; each store at INR10-12 crores capex plus inventory.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Customer-brand run-rate of ~INR400 crores is being exited with growth decelerating into H2, offsetting own-brand growth (39% in Q2; FY27 own-brand guide INR375 crores vs INR172 crores in H1).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Jean Dousset moving from ~25% to full in-house manufacturing over 12-18 months and FY28 store growth imply further spend, but no new capex figure or plant was announced and cash is earmarked for stores and acquisitions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Customer-brand FY27 revenue is guided at INR1,700-1,800 crores with run-rate reduction through year-end, so no upgrade signal; own-brand guidance of INR375 crores is the only firm upward marker.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth expected to decelerate in H2 as customer-brand exits continue, and forex losses of ~INR20 crores in the quarter on INR550-600 crores USD debt could weigh on reported profit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or brand launches were discussed beyond boutique openings.

rows.label: Working capital cycle cut toward ~180 days
rows.why: Cycle already cut 54 days YoY with ~INR417 crores of working capital avoided versus constant intensity, and TTM operating cash flow hit a record INR280 crores; target ~180 days.

rows.label: Net debt to ~INR100 crores by 2030
rows.why: Net debt already down 42% YoY to INR199 crores with TTM FCF of INR204 crores; but ~INR383 crores cash is held for acquisitions and next stores, so pace is uncertain.

rows.label: Own brands on track for INR375 crores FY27
rows.why: INR172 crores already booked in H1 (about 46% of the guide), with own-brand growth of 39% in Q2 and Jean Dousset above 50%.

tone.note: Management was confident on Jean Dousset store economics, cash flow and the working capital release, but evasive on consignment share, cost cuts and acquisition targets; analysts pressed on the H1 margin dip, forex losses on USD debt and why gross debt is carried.

oneOffs.what: Bullion sales INR146 crores in H1 are included in total revenue (INR1,474 crores, +37%) but excluded from operating revenue (INR1,329 crores, +25%); bullion flatters headline total revenue growth
~INR20 crores forex loss in Q2 FY27 hits profit (not revenue); PAT +92% in H1 partly reflects a weak year-ago base, not stated as a one-off

quality.why: Operating revenue growth of +20% in Q2 (INR639 crores vs INR532 crores) and +25% in H1 is driven by own brands (+39% in the quarter, INR172 crores in H1), but the customer-brand book is shrinking and decelerating, and bullion sales inflate headline total revenue growth to +37%.
